extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, civic-technology designers, and practitioners working on online public participation and e-rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and scholarly resources on designing, testing, moderating, and analysing online platforms for public participation in administrative rulemaking to achieve informed, inclusive, and useful public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support informed public discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and process of online engagement should support public discussion that is informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page summary: CeRI's work sought to discover how the design and process of online engagement can support public discussion that is informed. See related publications such as 'The Value of Words: Narrative as Evidence in Policymaking' and 'Rulemaking 2.0'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support inclusive public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and process should support public discussion that is inclusive, enabling diverse participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CeRI emphasizes inclusiveness as a core objective. Relevant items include 'Balancing Inclusion and “Enlightened Understanding” in Designing Online Civic Participation Systems' and papers from RegulationRoom field tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support insightful public discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and process should foster discussion that yields insight useful for policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initiative aimed for discussions that are 'insightful' in addition to informed and inclusive; see multiple papers on improving public participation quality (e.g., 'Rulemaking 2.0').

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance quantity ('more') versus quality ('better') of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform design must weigh achieving greater numbers of participants against achieving higher-quality, substantive contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflected in the paper title 'Designing an Online Civic Engagement Platform: Balancing "More" vs. "Better" Participation in Complex Public Policymaking' and 'Rulemaking 2.0'. Use interface and process choices to manage this tradeoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance inclusion with 'enlightened understanding'
rubrics_metrics.description: Design should navigate tensions between broad inclusion and fostering deep, deliberative understanding among participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on 'Balancing Inclusion and “Enlightened Understanding” in Designing Online Civic Participation Systems: Experiences from Regulation Room' — consider mechanisms that promote both broad access and substantive comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitative moderation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation should be facilitative—guiding, organizing, and supporting participation rather than merely policing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by the listed item 'Facilitative Moderation for Online Participation in eRulemaking' and the 'CeRI Moderator Protocol' file. Guidance implies concrete moderator protocols and techniques to encourage constructive input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interface design to improve input quality ('Better Inputs for Better Outcomes')
rubrics_metrics.description: User interface and interaction design choices can improve the quality and usefulness of public comments submitted through the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Better Inputs for Better Outcomes: Using the Interface to Improve e-Rulemaking' and 'Designing an Online Civic Engagement Platform' — use UI affordances and workflows to elicit more relevant and structured contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue categorization and analysis of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems should facilitate categorizing and analyzing comments by issue to make public input actionable for rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers such as 'Facilitating Issue Categorization & Analysis in Rulemaking' and 'A Study in Rule-Specific Issue Categorization for e-Rulemaking' provide methods and protocols for issue tagging and analytical workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natural language processing (NLP) and active learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply NLP, machine learning, and active learning techniques to identify substantive issues in public comments and to scale analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents on the page include 'Using Natural Language Processing to Improve eRulemaking [Project Highlight]', 'An eRulemaking Corpus: Identifying Substantive Issues in Public Comments', and 'Active Learning for e-Rulemaking: Public Comment Categorization'. These offer methodological guidance and corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-testing platforms during actual agency rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate platforms through field-testing in real agency rulemaking contexts to measure effectiveness and gather lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'RegulationRoom: Field-Testing An Online Public Participation Platform During USA Agency Rulemakings' and related RegulationRoom publications documenting deployment experiences and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and address barriers to platform adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize institutional, technological, and user-level barriers that impede adoption of participatory e-rulemaking platforms and develop strategies to overcome them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on 'Barriers to Participatory eRulemaking Platform Adoption: Lessons Learned from RegulationRoom' and other evaluations of platform deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide moderator protocols, manuals, and reproducible data
rubrics_metrics.description: Make moderator protocols, manuals, and comment datasets available to support replication, evaluation, and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists 'CeRI (Cornell eRulemaking) Moderator Protocol' and 'Comment Data from CeRI, 4-3-2017' under Data, Manuals, and Protocols, indicating the importance of documented procedures and shared data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat narrative as evidence in policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and evaluate narratives in comments as forms of evidence that can inform policymaking decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflected in the paper 'The Value of Words: Narrative as Evidence in Policymaking' — guidance suggests methods to surface and assess the evidentiary value of narratives in public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop frameworks for 'Rulemaking 2.0' to improve participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate conceptual and practical frameworks (Rulemaking 2.0) for understanding and improving public participation in rulemaking using online tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several publications (e.g., 'Rulemaking 2.0', 'Rulemaking 2.0: Understanding and Getting Better Public Participation') present high-level frameworks and recommendations for platform and process redesign aimed at better participation outcomes.
